title: Harness ensemble prompt curator and runner affinity for reproducible profile snapshots
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: When onboarding models we produce performance profiles that are brittle across runs because prompts and dataset sampling vary, runner assignment changes affinity, and artifacts are not snapshot-consistent. This causes flaky regressions during pinning and noisy comparisons across model versions.

Goal: Enhance the benchmark harness to produce deterministic, traceable performance profile snapshots by doing three coordinated things: (1) an ensemble prompt curation pipeline that canonicalizes and weights prompt variants; (2) runner affinity tagging + stable assignment so eval runners maintain consistent execution characteristics; (3) a snapshot publishing flow that archives dataset fingerprints, prompt-suite manifests, runner metadata, and seed state alongside published profiles.

Scope: Implement changes in harness dataset sampling, prompt pipeline, and runner orchestrator used by CI and the profile publisher. Backwards compatibility: existing profiles remain readable and we add a migration script that can rehydrate older snapshots with best-effort metadata.

Out of scope: UI console visualizations for the new snapshot metadata (this will be in a follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can produce a profile snapshot tarball that includes: dataset fingerprint (sha256), prompt-suite manifest (canonical text + variant ids + weights), runner-affinity file (runner ids and environment tags), and RNG seed state file

End-to-end flow: model onboarding job creates profile snapshots in CI; a subsequent run using the snapshot reproduces the original token distribution and latency P50 within a 5% tolerance for stable models
Prompt curation step deduplicates semantically identical prompts (using fuzzy hashing threshold) and produces deterministic ordering for the manifest
Runner affinity assignment is deterministic given a seed and cluster state hash; if runners are unavailable, fallback to labeled compatible runners and include fallback metadata
Publishing pipeline stores snapshot artifacts in artifact-bucket with lifecycle tag and exposes artifact path in profile metadata
Automated test coverage: unit tests for prompt canonicalizer, integration test for snapshot round-trip, and a regression test that flags divergent latency >10%
Migration script documented and validated on one historical profile bundle without data loss
design_decisions: Use combined lexical + simhash-based fingerprint for prompt deduplication to balance speed and semantic recall
Represent prompt-suite as an ordered list of variant groups; each variant group has stable id derived from namespace+hash
Encode runner affinity as a small JSON blob (flattened when stored in metadata) that contains runner_id, gpu_type, kernel-set, region_tag and a cluster_state_hash
Snapshot packaging: gzip tarball with top-level MANIFEST.txt linking artifact paths and checksums
Keep RNG seed deterministic via a named-seed generator seeded from model+dataset+timestamp, stored in snapshot manifest for replay
implementation_notes: Add new CLI flag `--emit-profile-snapshot` to harness runner (default off); when enabled, writes snapshot to /artifacts/snapshots/{model}-{version}-{ts}.tgz
Introduce prompt_canonicalizer module: responsibilities include normalizing whitespace, token-safe truncation, simhash fingerprinting, and producing stable variant ids
Runner orchestrator: annotate runner leases with `affinity_tag` and derive assignment via hashing of (job_id, seed, affinity_group) to achieve deterministic placement
Profile publisher: extend existing publishing API to attach `snapshot_artifact_path` and `snapshot_manifest_v=1` metadata to the profile object
Storage: leverage existing artifact-bucket with new prefix `snapshots/`; ensure server-side encryption is enabled and add lifecycle rule (90 days) for CI snapshots
Migration: add `tools/rehydrate_snapshot.sh` that can take legacy profile and emit best-effort manifest; include a smoke-check that validates presence of dataset fingerprint
risks: Deterministic runner assignment depends on cluster state stability; autoscaling churn could still change execution environment causing drift
Prompt deduplication may over-merge paraphrases if simhash threshold too aggressive, reducing coverage of edge cases
Snapshot storage costs could increase if we keep high-frequency CI snapshots; lifecycle policy mitigates but we need monitoring
Compatibility complexity when older consumer tooling expects profiles without snapshot fields
mitigation_plan: Include cluster_state_hash in snapshots so we can detect and record when runner drift occurred
Start with conservative simhash threshold (0.85) and run a tryout on 3000 prompt variants to calibrate before rollout
Apply lifecycle/retention and provide an opt-in full-retention flag for release snapshots only
Add schema versioning to snapshot manifest (`snapshot_manifest_v`) and keep reader tolerant to missing fields
testing_plan: Unit: prompt canonicalizer tests for normalization edge cases and stable id generation
Integration: harness profile generation pipeline with `--emit-profile-snapshot` and validate round-trip reproducibility in a replay job
Regression: nightly job that runs on a stable model and fails CI if token distribution or latency P50 deviates beyond thresholds
Chaos: synthetic runner churn test to measure how often deterministic assignment falls back and record fallback rate
notes: Perf benchmark: local runs show ~4% overhead for canonicalization on large prompt sets (10k prompts) — acceptable for weekly snapshots
